chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Abu Azza, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) passed by me while I was in the fifth circuit of the Tawaf. He said to me, 'Go, until we bid farewell to a man over there.' I said to him, 'But I am in the fifth circuit, so I should complete my seven circuits.' He said, 'Cut it, and remember it from where you cut it, until you return to the place from which you cut it, and build upon it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Tawaf if one has to stop midway for a necessary reason?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrates the principle of *qat'* (interruption) versus *naskh* (cancellation), ruling that a valid excuse allows the pilgrim to pause and resume from the exact point of departure rather than restarting the entire circuit. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on ease (*taysir*) and the preservation of the pilgrim's effort, distinguishing it from the Hanafi view which often requires restarting. The incident underscores the practical flexibility embedded in ritual worship, ensuring that obligations are fulfilled without undue hardship.
